links.outcome: In-hospital sepsis mortality and bundle compliance before versus after AI deployment, quasi-experimental
links.effect: 1.9% absolute reduction (17% relative) in in-hospital sepsis mortality (95% CI 0.3%-3.5%); 5.0% absolute increase in sepsis bundle compliance (95% CI 2.4%-8.0%); 4% reduction in 72-h SOFA change.
links.quote: The deployment of COMPOSER was significantly associated with a 1.9% absolute reduction (17% relative decrease) in in-hospital sepsis mortality (95% CI, 0.3%-3.5%), a 5.0% absolute increase (10% relative increase) in sepsis bundle compliance (95% CI, 2.4%-8.0%), and a 4% (95% CI, 1.1%-7.1%) reduction in 72-h SOFA change after sepsis onset in causal inference analysis.

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world deployment of a deep-learning sepsis prediction model (COMPOSER) via nurse-facing alerts on patient outcomes, but does not compare or evaluate a specific guardrail or deployment practice.
